name: docs-staleness
purpose: Find documentation that no longer describes the code it claims to describe.
corpus: One documentation section, paired with the code it describes.

state_schema.code_path: path of the code the section describes

criteria.true: the description matches the current code
criteria.false: the code has moved on, or the described thing is gone

misleads.instructions: Would a reader following this section take a wrong action?

still_needed.instructions: Is this section worth keeping at all, assuming it were corrected?

route.instructions: What should happen to this section?

criteria.edit: keep the section, correct the detail
criteria.delete: the thing it documents is gone
criteria.rewrite: the subject still exists but the section is wrong throughout

matches_code.calibration: CALIBRATED 2026-09-19 on 30 items: 22 real doc/code pairs from ~/src/conclave and ~/src/jev-mcp plus 8 controlled mismatches (a real doc section paired with real code it does not describe). WHAT HOLDS: the 8 controlled mismatches scored 0.02-0.06 and the 20 clear matches 0.40-0.93, so gross drift and clear agreement separate cleanly, and gate 0.25 sits in that empty band. WHAT DOES NOT: both genuinely subtle cases came out wrong. A doc section about a Claude auth probe paired with directory-grant code scored 0.47, leaning MATCHES when it does not. R22 paired with launch-retry.js scored 0.10, calling it stale when the two agree - R22 defers retry policy to the launch-failure classifier, which is what that file implements. At gate 0.25 that is 2 errors in 30, one in each direction, and both on the only hard cases in the set. Use this pack to sweep for obvious drift; do not use a score between 0.1 and 0.5 as evidence either way, and never let it close a subtle contradiction without a human reading both sides.

notes: Pair each section with the code it names. A doc audit that reads only the docs finds prose problems, not staleness.
